summary: Phase-1 Realms+Groups+Community Chats end-to-end testing. Backend pytest suite (14 tests, all PASS) covers: 8 seeded realms, public realm detail with online/member counts, chat list with main General Chat, idempotent join, paginated member list with full projection (user_id/username/display_name/avatar_url/presence_choice/is_online/role/joined_at/favorite), POST+GET messages with ascending created_at, admin rename success/403/400 cases, create-realm with owner auto-membership + _main_chat_id, regression for /api/admin/realm-pulse/overview, /api/hashtags/interest-cards, /api/admin/storage/status, /api/admin/moderation/copyright/queue, and the WebSocket /api/ws/community-chat/{chat_id}: 4401 on no token, 4404 on bad chat, chat:hello on accept, message:new broadcast between two clients. Frontend Playwright against the live preview URL with localStorage 'ourrealm.access' JWT confirmed all 11 required testids render on /realms/dj (realm-detail-dj, realm-chat-layout, community-chat-widget, community-chat-title='General Chat', community-chat-stream, community-chat-input, community-chat-send, community-members-panel, community-members-search, realm-customize, realm-banner-edit). Customize Community flow opens community-chat-title-modal, saving with new value closes the modal and updates community-chat-title in-place. Tab strip — Chat is the default selected tab; clicking realm-tab-feed hides the chat widget and keeps realm-detail-dj mounted (no page break). Banner editor opens BannerEditor modal. tfone correctly sees neither realm-customize nor community-chat-rename, but DOES see community-chat-widget. One backend bug found and fixed (ObjectId serialization in POST /api/communities/realms and /api/communities/groups — popped _id after insert_one).

critical_code_review_comments: FIXED: routers/communities.py — POST /communities/realms and POST /communities/groups were returning the freshly-inserted document which motor mutates with a BSON ObjectId. FastAPI then failed with 'ObjectId is not iterable' → 500. Added doc.pop('_id', None) right after insert_one in both endpoints. All other endpoints already project _id away via {'_id': 0}.

Good: WS /api/ws/community-chat/{chat_id} mirrors the presence WS pattern — calls await ws.accept() first then auth-checks and closes with 4401 (no token / bad token), 4404 (chat not found), 4403 (group non-member). The room-based fan-out in core/community_chat.py correctly uses an asyncio.Lock around the rooms dict and excludes the sender via exclude_ws when applicable.

Good: services/community_seed.py is idempotent (only seeds when realms collection is empty), creates the 8 expected realm ids + a 'General Chat' row per realm, and ensure_indexes builds the right composite indexes (community_type, community_id, user_id unique on memberships; chat_id+created_at on messages).
Good: ChatPatch.title uses Field(max_length=50) for upper bound (Pydantic 422) plus explicit 'Title must be 1–50 chars' 400 for empty strings.
Good: _is_admin treats 'stealth' as global founder/admin which matches the Phase-1 spec.

Frontend: CommunityChat.jsx, CommunityMembersPanel.jsx, RealmDetail.jsx all expose the documented data-testids cleanly. apiClient correctly reads localStorage 'ourrealm.access' (carried over from iter_23).

rca of the issue: One real backend bug found and fixed: POST /api/communities/realms (and /api/communities/groups) returned the Motor-mutated doc that contains a BSON ObjectId in _id, causing FastAPI to fail with TypeError("'ObjectId' object is not iterable") → 500 Internal Server Error. Root cause: insert_one mutates the dict in-place to add `_id`, and the endpoint then did `return {**doc, '_main_chat_id': chat['id']}`. Fix: doc.pop('_id', None) after insert_one in both create_realm and create_group. Verified by re-running pytest — test_create_realm_with_owner_and_main_chat now passes. No other ObjectId leaks because every other read uses `{'_id': 0}` projections.
